question.:question/problem: What is $\int {3}^{- x - 6}\,\text{d}x$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
If we let $u=- x - 6,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad -1\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {3}^{- x - 6}\,\text{d}x & =\int {3}^{u}\cdot (-1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =(-1)\int {3}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =(-1)\frac{{3}^{u}}{\ln 3}+C \\  & =- \frac{3^{- x - 6}}{\ln{(3 )}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-1$ | $1$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{1} 3\cdot {5}^{2 x - 1}\,\text{d}x & =\int_{-1}^{1} 3\cdot {5}^{u}\cdot (\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =(\frac{3}{2})\int_{-1}^{1} {5}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =(\frac{3}{2})(\frac{{5}^{u}}{\ln 5})|_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2 \ln{(5 )}})({5}^{1}-{5}^{-1}) \\  & =(\frac{3}{2 \ln{(5 )}})(5-\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{36}{5\ln 5}\end{aligned}
$$
